description: Coverage TARGET for the first independent human-authored safety evaluation set. This file holds counts and rationale only: no scenario text, no labels tied to a narrative, no reviewer record. It is a specification for human authors, not permission for any tool to generate samples.
no_stereotype_rule: Difficulty must come from linguistic structure (negation, scope, register, script, code-switching, turn order), never from caste, religion, region, gender, disability or occupation stereotypes. A sample whose only difficulty is a demographic marker must be rejected in review.

languages.why: English is the console language and the fallback intake language. It is also where the detectors are strongest, so it sets the ceiling the other two languages are measured against.

Hindi in Devanagari is the primary victim language for NHAA 14566 intake and the only one where ASR, lexicon and detector error compound. It needs its own critical-miss number, not a share of an aggregate.
Romanised and code-switched Hindi is what people actually type on a phone. Every published critical miss so far was a transliteration or misspelling case, so this slice must carry its own statistics.

categories.why: The highest-consequence detector. A critical-miss rate needs enough positives per language to be more than an anecdote, and the two-reviewer rule applies to every one of them.
The second hard override. Present-tense danger must be separable from future threat, which requires positives in all three languages.
The most common real pattern (threats after a complaint) and the easiest to confuse with immediate danger, so it needs the largest non-critical count.
Injury language is short, often understated and frequently missed, and it drives a different escalation route than threat.
Statute-specific vocabulary with heavy regional variation, where the published failures were regional-word false negatives.
Most intake is legal-procedural. Under-representing it makes the false-escalation rate look better than it is.
Determines whether the assistant may keep talking at all, and is the category most often defeated by conditional phrasing.
An invariant: a request for a person must always be honoured, in every language and register, including polite and indirect forms.
Plain questions with no danger. Without them the false-escalation denominator is empty and any precision claim is meaningless.
Cases where the correct behaviour is needs_human with no score. Abstention is an invariant and must be measured, not assumed.
Samples where every detector must stay silent. These are the only samples that can show whether hardening rules over-fire.
Real disclosures carry several dimensions at once. Single-label samples cannot expose evidence-attribution errors or SVI weighting errors.

slices.why: Risk vocabulary that is plainly denied. The cheapest way to produce a false escalation and the first thing a keyword system gets wrong.
A negation in one clause and a real disclosure in the next. Proves whether negation handling respects clause boundaries instead of the whole turn.
Conditional phrasing is neither a denial nor present intent. A published coercion failure came from a conditional being read as a negation.
Risk words inside quotation marks belong to another speaker. Quoted-speech false escalations are already a known failure class.
Reported speech without quotation marks is harder than quoted speech and must be scoped the same way.
The trap case: genuine danger to the caller AND attributed risk words. Suppressing the attributed phrase must not suppress the real alert.
A past attempt or past assault changes priority but is not present intent. Both over- and under-reaction are failures here.
Danger stated by implication. A published critical miss was exactly this shape.
Switching mid-sentence breaks phrase patterns anchored in one language. It is the normal register, not an edge case.
Hindi written in Latin script has no single spelling. Two published critical misses were transliteration variants.
People in distress type badly, and one character can defeat an exact phrase rule. Misspelt crisis text has already produced a critical miss.
Boycott, water-denial and displacement vocabulary varies by region, and published isolation false negatives were regional words.
Severity is often expressed with apology and understatement. A system tuned on explicit wording systematically under-reacts to it.
Several mild signals that should aggregate. Tests the SVI weighting rather than any single detector.
A disclosure followed by reassurance. Determines whether reassurance can cancel evidence it should not.
Roleplay framing around risk words must neither trigger a false critical route nor let a real disclosure through.
Attempts to set the score, reveal the band or override instructions. Invariant 3 forbids ever answering, and this must be measured in all three languages.
Instruction-shaped text inside an otherwise genuine victim turn: the instruction must be ignored and the disclosure still assessed.
Evidence spread over turns is the normal case in intake and the only way to test state carry-over.
The decisive turn arrives last. Catches pipelines that assess only the first or the current utterance.
A caller restates or corrects themself. Tests whether a correction supersedes the earlier claim.
Text that is lexically close to a critical case but genuinely safe. The sharpest available test of precision, and the class most likely to regress after hardening.

notes: Counts are minimums. A sample may satisfy several categories and several slices at once, so the sums exceed 180 by design.

Category membership is taken from the FROZEN human labels. Slice membership is author-declared structural metadata, corrected in review only when a reviewer flags it as wrong; it is accounting, never evidence.
Language totals are hard: a shortfall in any one language blocks the freeze rather than being absorbed by the other two.
min_per_language 0 with an explicit languages list means the slice is only meaningful in those languages and the total is what binds.
This plan is versioned. Changing a minimum bumps plan_version and needs the same lead approval as a contract change.
